```{r}
library(rstan)
library(bayesplot)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)
library(parallel)

rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)
# save compiled Stan model automatically
# compilation is slow --> need to do it only once and is reused on future runs

options(mc.cores = 1)
# use 1 CPU core per chain, overrode later when we do parallel mode
# --> each worker runs on 1 core --> no problem with shared cores

if (!dir.exists("output")) dir.create("output")
# make output1 folder or store in that folder if already there

## simulation grid
I_vals <- c(40, 80, 160) # number of participants to test
J_vals <- c(40, 80, 160) # trials per participant per condition to test
N_sim  <- 30 # independent simulation replications per I×J combination
K      <- 2 # how many conditions
# 3x3x30 = 270 simulations

## true parameters, simulation generates data from this
# can they be recovered from data? 
# stan only retrieves data generated from them 
true <- list(
  mu_nu    = 0.4, # mean/intercept for drift
  b1_nu    = 0.1, # how much the covariate shifts drift in cond 1 
  b2_nu    = 0.3, # difference cond 2 to cond 1 
  mu_alpha = 1.5, # average boundary separation in condition 1
  b_alpha  = 0.2, # condition 2 boundary is on average 0.2 wider 
  mu_tau   = 0.3, # average non-decision time in condition 1 (in seconds)
  b_tau    = 0.25,   # condition 2 NDT is 0.25 seconds longer 
  sigma_nu    = 0.3, # how much individuals vary in (log-)drift (SD log scale)
  sigma_alpha = 0.25, # how much individuals vary in boundary (SD)
  sigma_tau   = 0.15, # how much individuals vary in NDT (SD)
  sigma_v     = 0.2 # how much individuals vary in cond effect on boundary sep (SD of random slope)
)

## function takes observed data (how many correct, trials, mean RTs, RT variances) and computes point estimates of nu, alpha and tau
# using the EZ equations
# used only in "pilot" to derive priors 
ez_point_estimates <- function(C_arr, J_arr, MRT_mat, VRT_mat, I, K) {
# inputs:
# C_arr: matrix of correct responses, I rows × K columns
# J_arr: matrix of trials (same)
# MRT_mat: matrix of mean RTs of correct responses
# VRT_mat: matrix of RT variances
# I: number of participants
# K: number of conditions
  nu_hat    <- matrix(NA, I, K)
  alpha_hat <- matrix(NA, I, K)
  tau_hat   <- matrix(NA, I, K)
  # three empty I×K matrices
  
  for (i in seq_len(I)) { # for each participant (seq_len(I) safer than 1:I)
    for (k in seq_len(K)) { # in each condition 
      
      Pc  <- C_arr[i, k] / J_arr[i, k] # proportion correct for participant i in condition k (correct responses divided by total trials)
      
      Pc  <- max(min(Pc, 1 - 1 / (2 * J_arr[i, k])), 1 / (2 * J_arr[i, k])) # Pc away from exactly 0 or 1 bc the EZ equations break down at         exact accuracy = 1 or 0 bc log of 0 is undefined) --> took smallest proportion possible that was not zero with J trials (1/(2*J))
      
      mrt <- MRT_mat[i, k] # mrt is matrix of i and k for mean of correct responses
      vrt <- VRT_mat[i, k] # vrt same for variance 
      
      if (is.na(mrt) || is.na(vrt) || vrt <= 0) next # skip cell if mean RT or variance is NA or variance is zero or negative (bc then we           cannot compute the estimates)
      
      L   <- log(Pc / (1 - Pc)) # logit transformation so the log-odds of being correct 
      # boundary × drift, alpha = L / nu 
      # e.g.,  Pc = 0.8 --> L = log(0.8/0.2) = log(4) so about 1.39
      
      
      nu4 <- L * (Pc^2 * L - Pc * L + Pc - 0.5) / vrt
      # getting v(hoch 4) from the EZ inversion formulas
      # rearrange EZ RT variance equation to isolate nu 
      # nu^4 = L × (Pc^2 × L − Pc × L + Pc − 0.5) / VRT --> solve for nu
      # alpha  = L / nu --> get alpha
      # tau  = MRT − (alpha / 2xnu) × (2Pc − 1) --> get tau
       
      if (is.na(nu4) || nu4 <= 0) next # skip if  nu4 is negative or missing
      
      nu_hat[i, k]    <- sign(Pc - 0.5) * nu4^(1/4)
      # drift rate estimate
      # sign(Pc - 0.5) is +1 if accuracy > 50% (positive drift toward correct boundary) and −1 otherwise 
      # sign returns 1 for positive values, -1 for negative values, and 0 for zero
      
      alpha_hat[i, k] <- L / nu_hat[i, k]
      # boundary sep estimate from EZ --> boundary = log-odds / drift rate
      
      tau_hat[i, k]   <- mrt - (alpha_hat[i, k] / (2 * nu_hat[i, k])) * (2 * Pc - 1)
      # NDT estimate -->  mean RT - decision time component ((alpha_hat[i, k] / (2 * nu_hat[i, k])) * (2 * Pc - 1)) = NDT
    }
  }
  list(nu = nu_hat, alpha = alpha_hat, tau = tau_hat) # put all three matrices into list
}




## function takes EZ estimates from pilot data and turns them into prior hyperparameters (that we put into stan then)
derive_priors <- function(ez) { # the input is "ez" so the list returned by by "ez_point_estimates"
  
  nu_vals    <- as.vector(ez$nu[!is.na(ez$nu) & ez$nu > 0])
  # nu_vals = vector of all valid drift estimates
  # ez$nu = I×K matrix but as single vector
  # !is.na(ez$nu) and ez$nu > 0 --> keep only cells that are not missing and positive 
  
  alpha_vals <- as.vector(ez$alpha[!is.na(ez$alpha) & ez$alpha > 0])
  # same for boundary sep 
  
  tau_vals   <- as.vector(ez$tau[!is.na(ez$tau) & ez$tau > 0.05])
  # and for NDT but here its above 0.05 and not only positive
  
  log_nu_vals <- log(nu_vals)
  # convert drift estimates to log scale bc nu is log-normally distributed in model so the priors have to be placed on log(nu)
  
  nu_sd    <- min(max(sd(log_nu_vals), 0.3), 1.5)
  # compute SD of log(nu) across participants and conditions in pilot data
  # ensure its above 0.3 and maximum 1.5 --> robustness for pilot
  
  alpha_sd <- min(max(sd(alpha_vals),  0.2), 1.0)
  # same here but with diff values
  tau_sd   <- min(max(sd(tau_vals),    0.1), 0.5)

  list(
    beta_nu    = matrix(c(mean(log_nu_vals), 0,       0,
                          nu_sd,             nu_sd,   nu_sd),   
                        nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),
    # 2×3 matrix
    # row 1 = prior means for [intercept, covariate slope, condition slope] of nu
    # row 2 = prior SDs
    # intercept has mean(log_nu_vals) as prior mean so it is centred on what the pilot data says
    # slopes have 0 bc we dont know direction
    # byrow = TRUE fills matrix row by row 
    
    beta_alpha = matrix(c(mean(alpha_vals), 0,
                          alpha_sd * 2,     alpha_sd * 2),
                        nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),
    # for alpha its 2x2 and for tau too
    beta_tau   = matrix(c(mean(tau_vals),   0,
                          tau_sd * 2,       tau_sd * 2),
                        nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),
    
    sigma_nu    = c(nu_sd,    nu_sd / 2), # prior for population SD of log-drift = normal dist with mean = nu_sd and SD = nu_sd/2
    sigma_alpha = c(alpha_sd, alpha_sd / 2), 
    sigma_tau   = c(tau_sd,   tau_sd / 2),
    sigma_v     = c(nu_sd * 0.3, nu_sd) # random slope variability --> nu_sd * 0.3 and nu_sd --> much uncertainty, wide prior
  )
}

## function derives the priors from pilot aka 
# that simulates separate set of pilot participants, generates data from the true parameters, and runs EZ formulas on them and then calls the function derive_priors to get the prior hyperparameters
derive_priors_from_pilot <- function(J_per, true, I_pilot = 20) { 
  # J_per = trials per condition in the pilot, true = true parameters, I_pilot = how many pilot participants so 20
  K          <- 2
  cond_dummy <- c(0, 1)
  # cond 1 --> dummy variable 0 (reference)
  # cond 2 --> 1 (treatment)
  # multiplied by condition effect -->effect is zero for cond 1 and there is effect for cond 2
  
  x_p      <- rnorm(I_pilot, 0, 1)
  true_v_p <- rnorm(I_pilot, 0, true$sigma_v)
  # draw pilot ppns covariate values (x_p) from standard normal
  # draw pilot ppns random slope values (true_v_p) from Normal(0, sigma_v)
  # each ppn has own x and v
  
  # empty data matrices for the pilot participants --> filled by simulation 
  J_p   <- matrix(J_per, I_pilot, K) # every cell is filled with J_per --> e.g., if J_per = 80 and I_pilot = 20, this is a 20×2 matrix of 80s
  C_p   <- matrix(NA_integer_, I_pilot, K) # placeholder I_pilot × K matrix for integers (how many correct)
  MRT_p <- matrix(NA_real_,    I_pilot, K) # same but real number because MRT
  VRT_p <- matrix(NA_real_,    I_pilot, K) # same bc VRT
  
  
  for (i in seq_len(I_pilot)) { # for ppn i
    for (k in seq_len(K)) { # in cond k 
      mean_nu_ik    <- true$mu_nu + true$b1_nu * x_p[i] + true$b2_nu * cond_dummy[k]
      # computes log-scale mean for participant i in condition k
      # = intercept + covariate effect * x + condition effect * dummy
      # for cond 1 (dummy = 0) condition effect * dummy is gone (0)
      
      mean_alpha_ik <- true$mu_alpha + (true$b_alpha + true_v_p[i]) * cond_dummy[k]
      # boundary sep mean per person per cond
      # = intercept + (average condition effect + this ppns adjustment) * dummy
      # again, 0 in cond 1, in cond 2 the ppns own random slope shifts boundary adjustment
      
      mean_tau_ik   <- true$mu_tau + true$b_tau * cond_dummy[k]
      # NDT mean per person
      
      repeat { a <- rnorm(1, mean_alpha_ik, true$sigma_alpha)
               if (a > 0.1 && a < 3.0) { ap <- a; break } }
      # repeat loops forever until "break" hits
      # draw alpha from normal dist and check whether it falls in the valid range, continues until valid draw and saves it (under ap)
      
      
      np <- exp(rnorm(1, mean_nu_ik, true$sigma_nu))
      # draws log-drift from normal(mean_nu_ik, sigma_nu) but exponentiated (makes it always positive so no repeating necessary)
      
      repeat { t <- rnorm(1, mean_tau_ik, true$sigma_tau)
               if (t > 0.05) { tp <- t; break } }
      # same for tau what we did for alpha
      
      
      e      <- exp(-ap * np)
      pi_c   <- 1 / (1 + e)
      mu_rt  <- tp + (ap / (2 * np)) * ((1 - e) / (1 + e))
      sig2rt <- (ap / (2 * np^3)) * ((1 - 2*ap*np*e - e^2) / (1 + e)^2)
      # ez equations 
      # given tau, alpha and nu, predict: e, predicted proportion correct, predicted mean RT for correct ones and predicted variance 
      
      C_ik <- rbinom(1, J_per, pi_c)
      C_ik <- max(1L, min(C_ik, J_per - 1L))
      # draw number of correct responses from binomial dist (J_per trials, probability pi_c)
      # [1, J−1] again to not allow 0 or all correct because EZ formulas break then 
      # 1L = integer 1

      
      MRT_p[i, k] <- rnorm(1, mu_rt, sqrt(sig2rt / C_ik))
      # draw observed mean RT from normal dist centred on true mean RT
      # SD is standard error of the mean RT --> gets smaller when more correct trials
      
      VRT_p[i, k] <- max(rnorm(1, sig2rt, sqrt(2 * sig2rt^2 / max(C_ik-1,1))), 1e-6)
      # draw observed RT variance from normal centred on true variance
      # SD --> chi-squared approximation for sample variance
      # max(..., 1e-6) so never gets negative 
      # max(C_ik-1, 1) so its not diveded by zero when only 1 correct response
      
      C_p[i, k]   <- C_ik
    }
  }
  ez <- ez_point_estimates(C_p, J_p, MRT_p, VRT_p, I_pilot, K)
  derive_priors(ez) # runs earlier function on those estimates
}



## simulation and Stan fit
## function takes one set (I, J, priors), simulates dataset from true parameters, fits stan model and returns results
run_one <- function(I, J_per, true, model, priors,
                    rhat_threshold     = 1.05,
                    hopeless_threshold = 10,
                    iter1 = 1000, warmup1 = 300,
                    iter2 = 3000, warmup2 = 1000) {
  # I: number of ppns
  # J_per: trials per ppn per cond
  # true: "true parameter" list
  # model: stan model 
  # priors: already computed prior hyperparameters for this J value
  # rhat_threshold: if any Rhat exceeds this it triggers a longer refit 
  # hopeless_threshold: if Rhat exceeds 10 the fit is seen as degenerate and excluded
  # iter1 and warmup1: iterations and warmup for first run
  # iter2 and warmup2: iterations and warmup for second run if first didnt converge
  
  
  K          <- 2
  cond_dummy <- c(0, 1)
  prs <- priors #rename
  
  x      <- rnorm(I, 0, 1)
  true_v <- rnorm(I, 0, true$sigma_v)
  # draw ppns covariate values and random slopes
  # --> "true" individual differences 
  
  
  X_nu    <- array(NA_real_, dim = c(I, K, 3))
  X_alpha <- array(NA_real_, dim = c(I, K, 2))
  X_tau   <- array(NA_real_, dim = c(I, K, 2))
  # 3 empty arrays (I × K × predictors) --> design matrices mit 3 and 2 dimensions --> tell stan what predictors each ppn in each cond has
  
  
  for (i in seq_len(I)) { # for ppn i
    for (k in seq_len(K)) { # in cond k
      X_nu[i, k, ]    <- c(1, x[i], cond_dummy[k]) 
      # nu predictor row is [1, x_i, cond_dummy_k]: 1 (intercept), covariate value, 0 or 1 depending on cond
      # stan multiplies row vector by [beta_nu[1], beta_nu[2], beta_nu[3]] --> we get the linear predictor for this cell
      X_alpha[i, k, ] <- c(1, cond_dummy[k])
      X_tau[i, k, ]   <- c(1, cond_dummy[k])
      # alpha and tau only have intercept + condition dummy 
    }
  }
  # true parameter generation
  # same as pilot above but this time different participants (the "actual" ones)
  alpha_true <- matrix(NA_real_, I, K)
  nu_true    <- matrix(NA_real_, I, K)
  tau_true   <- matrix(NA_real_, I, K)
  # again 3 empty arrays
  
  for (i in seq_len(I)) { # for ppn i
    for (k in seq_len(K)) { # in cond k 
      mean_nu_ik    <- true$mu_nu + true$b1_nu * x[i] + true$b2_nu * cond_dummy[k]
      # again log-scale mean for participant i in condition k
      
      mean_alpha_ik <- true$mu_alpha + (true$b_alpha + true_v[i]) * cond_dummy[k]
      # again boundary sep mean per person per cond
      
      mean_tau_ik   <- true$mu_tau + true$b_tau * cond_dummy[k]
      # and again NDT mean per ppn per cond 
      
      repeat { a <- rnorm(1, mean_alpha_ik, true$sigma_alpha)
               if (a > 0.1 && a < 3.0) { alpha_true[i, k] <- a; break } }
      # again draw alpha from normal dist --> repeat until valid for alpha 
      
      nu_true[i, k] <- exp(rnorm(1, mean_nu_ik, true$sigma_nu))
      # draw nu and again bc its exponentiated we dont need to repeat 
      
      repeat { t <- rnorm(1, mean_tau_ik, true$sigma_tau)
               if (t > 0.05) { tau_true[i, k] <- t; break } }
      # again also draw tau and repeat until valid 
    }
  }
  
  J_mat   <- matrix(J_per, I, K) # same as before: J_mat is filled with J_per (same number of trials for everyone)
  C_mat   <- matrix(NA_integer_, I, K) # and these are placeholder matrices again
  MRT_mat <- matrix(NA_real_,    I, K)
  VRT_mat <- matrix(NA_real_,    I, K)
  
  for (i in seq_len(I)) { # for ppn i
    for (k in seq_len(K)) { # in cond k
      # retrieve the true parameters for this cell, call them: a = boundary sep, v = drift, tau = NDT
      a <- alpha_true[i, k]; v <- nu_true[i, k]; tau <- tau_true[i, k]
      e      <- exp(-a * v) # when drift and boundary sep are large, a*v is large, e is near 0, when small, e is near 1
      pi_c   <- 1 / (1 + e) # predicted proportion correct from EZ
      
      mu_rt  <- tau + (a / (2 * v)) * ((1 - e) / (1 + e)) # predicted mean RT of correct responses
      # NDT + average time accumulator takes to hit correct boundary
      
      sig2rt <- (a / (2 * v^3)) * ((1 - 2*a*v*e - e^2) / (1 + e)^2) # predicted RT variance 
      # gets larger when drift is slow 
      
      # parameters are generated, now observed data generation
      # same as before, generate observed correct trials, mean RTs, RT variances from the true parameters
      C_ik <- rbinom(1, J_per, pi_c)
      C_ik <- max(1L, min(C_ik, J_per - 1L))
      # again draw observed number of correct responses from binomial dist, J_per trials, each with probability pi_c
      # again [1, J_per−1]to not allow 0 or all correct because then the formulas break
      
      MRT_mat[i, k] <- rnorm(1, mu_rt, sqrt(sig2rt / C_ik)) # as before
      VRT_mat[i, k] <- max(rnorm(1, sig2rt, sqrt(2 * sig2rt^2 / max(C_ik-1,1))), 1e-6) # as before
      C_mat[i, k]   <- C_ik # as before 
    }
  }
  
  
  stan_data <- list(
    I = I, K = K,
    P_nu = 3L, P_alpha = 2L, P_tau = 2L,
    J = J_mat, C = C_mat, MRT = MRT_mat, VRT = VRT_mat,
    X_nu = X_nu, X_alpha = X_alpha, X_tau = X_tau,
    prior_beta_nu     = prs$beta_nu,
    prior_beta_alpha  = prs$beta_alpha,
    prior_beta_tau    = prs$beta_tau,
    prior_sigma_nu    = prs$sigma_nu,
    prior_sigma_alpha = prs$sigma_alpha,
    prior_sigma_tau   = prs$sigma_tau,
    prior_sigma_v     = prs$sigma_v
  )
  # pack everything into list for Stan
  # dimensions, observed data matrices, design matrices, prior hyperparameters
  # "L" means its integers not floating numbers --> because of stan being bitchy otherwise if we only write e.g., 3
  
  
  
  group_pars <- c(
    paste0("beta_nu[",    seq_len(3), "]"),
    paste0("beta_alpha[", seq_len(2), "]"),
    paste0("beta_tau[",   seq_len(2), "]"),
    "sigma_nu", "sigma_alpha", "sigma_tau", "sigma_v"
  )
  # character vector of the parameter names stan uses for the group-level parameters
  # paste0("beta_nu[", 1:3, "]") --> gets us c("beta_nu[1]", "beta_nu[2]", "beta_nu[3]")
  # to extract Rhat values from stan summary later
  

  

  hopeless <- function(fit) {
    rh <- tryCatch(summary(fit)$summary[group_pars, "Rhat"], error = function(e) NA_real_)
    any(is.na(rh)) || any(is.nan(rh)) || any(is.infinite(rh)) ||
      any(rh > hopeless_threshold, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  # helper function for hopeless cases 
  # tryCatch runs what is inside of it and catches errors and then returns NA
  # extracts Rhats and returns TRUE if values are missing, NaN, infinite, or above 10 
  # then they are broken 
  
  
  fit <- tryCatch(
    sampling(model, data = stan_data,
             iter = iter1, warmup = warmup1, chains = 4, cores = 1, refresh = 0,
             control = list(adapt_delta = 0.85, max_treedepth = 10)),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  # drawing MCMC samples with sampling rstan function
  # runs 4 independent chains 
  # refresh = 0 supresses stans progress output
  # adapt_delta --> step size (higher --> more careful --> slower)
  # max_treedepth --> how deep goes sampler tree
  # when stan crashes --> tryCatch catches error and returns NULL so it doesnt crash
  
  if (is.null(fit))  return(list(status = "error"))
  if (hopeless(fit)) return(list(status = "excluded", reason = "degenerate_fit1"))
  # if stan crashes --> this error is returned
  # if fit has Rhat > 10 this exclusion message is returned
  # return() exits function directly and gives out message
  
  
  rhat_max  <- max(summary(fit)$summary[group_pars, "Rhat"], na.rm = TRUE)
  converged <- "first_fit"
  if (rhat_max > rhat_threshold) {
    # extract the worst Rhat of group-level parameters
    # if > 1.05 --> fit hasn't converged well enough 
    # --> has to rerun with more iterations
    # shows this message in console so I know
    message(sprintf("Refit triggered (I=%d, J=%d) — Rhat = %.2f", I, J_per, rhat_max))
    
    
    fit <- tryCatch(
      sampling(model, data = stan_data,
               iter = iter2, warmup = warmup2, chains = 4, cores = 1, refresh = 0,
               control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 12)),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )
    # refit with iter2 = 3000 warmup2 = 1000 and adapt_delta = 0.95 and max_treedepth = 12
    # stricter 
    
    if (is.null(fit))  return(list(status = "error")) # check again like before
    if (hopeless(fit)) return(list(status = "excluded", reason = "degenerate_refit"))
    rhat_max  <- max(summary(fit)$summary[group_pars, "Rhat"], na.rm = TRUE) # also Rhats
    converged <- "refit"
    if (rhat_max > rhat_threshold)
      return(list(status = "excluded", reason = "non_converged"))
  }
  # if it still does not converge --> exclude
  
  
  s <- summary(fit)$summary
  # summary matrix --> 1 row per parameter (columns for mean, SD, quantiles, Rhat, n_eff)
  
  
  group_results <- data.frame(
    # for plotting results later --> data frame table,  one row per group-level parameter
    # row has I and J of this run, parameter name, true value, posterior mean estimate and the used prior 
    # aggregated across all simulation runs 
    I = I, J = J_per,
    param = c("mu_nu", "b1_nu", "b2_nu",
              "mu_alpha", "b_alpha",
              "mu_tau", "b_tau",
              "sigma_nu", "sigma_alpha", "sigma_tau", "sigma_v"),
    true_val = c(true$mu_nu,    true$b1_nu,    true$b2_nu,
                 true$mu_alpha, true$b_alpha,
                 true$mu_tau,   true$b_tau,
                 true$sigma_nu, true$sigma_alpha, true$sigma_tau, true$sigma_v),
    estimate = c(
      s["beta_nu[1]",    "mean"], s["beta_nu[2]",    "mean"], s["beta_nu[3]",  "mean"],
      s["beta_alpha[1]", "mean"], s["beta_alpha[2]", "mean"],
      s["beta_tau[1]",   "mean"], s["beta_tau[2]",   "mean"],
      s["sigma_nu",      "mean"], s["sigma_alpha",   "mean"],
      s["sigma_tau",     "mean"], s["sigma_v",       "mean"]
    ),
    prior_mean = c(
      prs$beta_nu[1,1],    prs$beta_nu[1,2],    prs$beta_nu[1,3],
      prs$beta_alpha[1,1], prs$beta_alpha[1,2],
      prs$beta_tau[1,1],   prs$beta_tau[1,2],
      prs$sigma_nu[1], prs$sigma_alpha[1], prs$sigma_tau[1], prs$sigma_v[1]
    ),
    prior_sd = c(
      prs$beta_nu[2,1],    prs$beta_nu[2,2],    prs$beta_nu[2,3],
      prs$beta_alpha[2,1], prs$beta_alpha[2,2],
      prs$beta_tau[2,1],   prs$beta_tau[2,2],
      prs$sigma_nu[2], prs$sigma_alpha[2], prs$sigma_tau[2], prs$sigma_v[2]
    ),
    converged = converged,
    rhat_max  = rhat_max,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
 
  
  
  
  v_results <- data.frame(
    I = I, J = J_per,
    participant = seq_len(I),
    true_v = true_v,
    est_v  = s[paste0("v[", seq_len(I), "]"), "mean"]
  )
  # 1 row per participant with their true random slope and estimated random slope
  # paste0("v[", 1:I, "]") --> generates stan parameter names v[1], ... v[I]
  
  alpha_est <- matrix(NA_real_, I, K)
  nu_est    <- matrix(NA_real_, I, K)
  tau_est   <- matrix(NA_real_, I, K)
  # posterior mean estimates from stan --> estimation for each value
  # empty matrices with row length I and column length K to fill with estimated alpha, nu and tau 
  # mirroring alpha_true, nu_true, tau_true
  
  for (i in seq_len(I)) { # for ppn i
    for (k in seq_len(K)) { # in cond k
      alpha_est[i, k] <- s[paste0("alpha[", i, ",", k, "]"), "mean"] 
      nu_est[i, k]    <- s[paste0("nu[",    i, ",", k, "]"), "mean"]
      tau_est[i, k]   <- s[paste0("tau[",   i, ",", k, "]"), "mean"]
      # s = stan summary matrix from before  with 1 row per parameter
      # individual parameters are then called alpha[1,1], alpha[1,2], alpha[2,1] etc
      # paste0("alpha[", i, ",", k, "]") makes this exact thing --> so for i=3, k=2 its alpha[3,2]
      # the mean column extracts the posterior mean for this ppn in this condition
      # whole result is stored in alpha_est[i, k]
      # same for the tau and nu
    }
  }
  
  indiv_results <- data.frame(
    #  individual results data frame
    I = I, J = J_per,
    # every row gets the I and row of its run
    condition  = rep(seq_len(K), each = I), # condition column
    # seq_len(K) --> c(1, 2)
    # rep(..., each = I) repeats every value I times so --> c(1,1,...,1, 2,2,...,2)
    # as.vector() on a matrix reads column by column --> so the first I rows correspond to cond 1 and the next I rows to cond 2
    
    true_alpha = as.vector(alpha_true), est_alpha = as.vector(alpha_est),
    true_nu    = as.vector(nu_true),    est_nu    = as.vector(nu_est),
    true_tau   = as.vector(tau_true),   est_tau   = as.vector(tau_est)
    # as.vector() makes the I*K matrix into a vector of length I*K that first rerads column 1 and  then column 2
    # true_alpha next to est_alpha in data frame --> every row has true value and estimate for the same cell (ppn + cond)
    # need this to plot individual results later
  )
    # data frame has I*K rows per simulation run, one for each combination of participant and condition, and columns for the simulation design     (I, J), which condition it was, and the true and estimated value of each parameter
  list(status = "ok", group = group_results, v = v_results, indiv = indiv_results,
       priors_used = prs, rhat_max = rhat_max, converged = converged)
  # status = ok is later for checking successful runs and bad ones
  
}


## compile Stan model
cache_file <- paste0(tools::file_path_sans_ext(
  "corrected_model_w_cond_and_random_slope.stan"), ".rds")
if (file.exists(cache_file)) file.remove(cache_file)
# forces a fresh recompile --> not using old compiled version if edited 

## derive priors once per J value 
set.seed(42) # reproducible
priors_by_J <- setNames( 
  lapply(J_vals, function(j) derive_priors_from_pilot(j, true, I_pilot = 20)), 
  # applies function to each element of J_vals --> returns list with 3 results
  as.character(J_vals) # names the list elements "20", etc so they can be looked up again
)
# priors_by_J[["20"]], priors_by_J[["60"]] and priors_by_J[["160"]] each contains set of prior hyperparameters that are derived from 20 participants at that J



## parallel simulation
jobs      <- expand.grid(I = I_vals, J = J_vals, sim = seq_len(N_sim))
# expand.grid creates 3 I values × 3 J values × 60 simulations = data frame with 540 rows --> one per job

jobs_list <- split(jobs, seq_len(nrow(jobs)))
## splits data frame into a list of one-row data frames, each worker gets one element of list

cl <- makeCluster(detectCores() - 1)
## makes cluster of worker processes --> detectCores() --> how many CPU cores --> uses all besides one

clusterSetRNGStream(cl, 42)
## parallel safe random number streams for all workers, seeded 
## otherwise all workers would use the same random numbers

clusterExport(cl, varlist = c("run_one", "derive_priors_from_pilot",
                              "ez_point_estimates", "derive_priors",
                              "true", "priors_by_J"))
# sends objects from session to every worker
# workers = separate processes with empty environments without knowledge from session 


clusterEvalQ(cl, {
  library(rstan)
  library(dplyr)
  rstan_options(auto_write = FALSE)
  options(mc.cores = 1)
  ez_cond <<- stan_model("corrected_model_w_cond_and_random_slope.stan")
})
## each worker loads stan, compiles model into ez_cond, and sets mc.cores = 1 so stan doesn't use multiple cores from within a worker
## "<<-" assigns to the global environment of the worker 



results_list <- parLapply(cl, jobs_list, function(row) {

})
# parallel lappply

stopCluster(cl)

saveRDS(results_list, file = "output/simulation_results.rds")
```

```{r back to normals and different parameters and safeguarded sigma_rt^2}
# check for correct stan file!!
library(rstan)
library(bayesplot)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)
library(parallel)

rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)
# save compiled Stan model automatically
# compilation is slow --> need to do it only once and is reused on future runs

options(mc.cores = 1)
# use 1 CPU core per chain, overrode later when we do parallel mode
# --> each worker runs on 1 core --> no problem with shared cores

if (!dir.exists("output_new")) dir.create("output_new")
# make output folder or store in that folder if already there

## simulation grid
I_vals <- c(40, 160) # number of participants to test
J_vals <- c(40, 160) # trials per participant per condition to test
N_sim  <- 5 # independent simulation replications per I×J combination
K      <- 2 # how many conditions
# 3x3x30 = 270 simulations

## true parameters, simulation generates data from this
# can they be recovered from data?
# stan only retrieves data generated from them
true <- list(
  mu_nu    = 0.4, # mean/intercept for drift 
  b1_nu    = 0.1, # how much the covariate shifts drift in cond 1 
  b2_nu    = 0.3, # difference cond 2 to cond 1 
  mu_alpha = 1.5, # average boundary separation in condition 1
  b_alpha  = 0.2, # condition 2 boundary is on average 0.2 wider
  mu_tau   = 0.3, # average non-decision time in condition 1 (in seconds)
  b_tau    = 0.25,   # condition 2 NDT is 0.25 seconds longer
  sigma_nu    = 0.3, # how much individuals vary in drift (SD, raw scale)
  sigma_alpha = 0.25, # how much individuals vary in boundary (SD)
  sigma_tau   = 0.15, # how much individuals vary in NDT (SD)
  sigma_v     = 0.2 # how much individuals vary in cond effect on boundary sep (SD of random slope)
)

## function takes observed data (how many correct, trials, mean RTs, RT variances) and computes point estimates of nu, alpha and tau
# using the EZ equations
# used only in "pilot" to derive priors
ez_point_estimates <- function(C_arr, J_arr, MRT_mat, VRT_mat, I, K) {
# inputs:
# C_arr: matrix of correct responses, I rows × K columns
# J_arr: matrix of trials (same)
# MRT_mat: matrix of mean RTs of correct responses
# VRT_mat: matrix of RT variances
# I: number of participants
# K: number of conditions
  nu_hat    <- matrix(NA, I, K)
  alpha_hat <- matrix(NA, I, K)
  tau_hat   <- matrix(NA, I, K)
  # three empty I×K matrices

  for (i in seq_len(I)) { # for each participant (seq_len(I) safer than 1:I)
    for (k in seq_len(K)) { # in each condition

      Pc  <- C_arr[i, k] / J_arr[i, k] # proportion correct for participant i in condition k (correct responses divided by total trials)

      Pc  <- max(min(Pc, 1 - 1 / (2 * J_arr[i, k])), 1 / (2 * J_arr[i, k])) # Pc away from exactly 0 or 1 bc the EZ equations break down at         exact accuracy = 1 or 0 bc log of 0 is undefined) --> took smallest proportion possible that was not zero with J trials (1/(2*J))

      mrt <- MRT_mat[i, k] # mrt is matrix of i and k for mean of correct responses
      vrt <- VRT_mat[i, k] # vrt same for variance

      if (is.na(mrt) || is.na(vrt) || vrt <= 0) next # skip cell if mean RT or variance is NA or variance is zero or negative (bc then we           cannot compute the estimates)

      L   <- log(Pc / (1 - Pc)) # logit transformation so the log-odds of being correct
      # boundary × drift, alpha = L / nu
      # e.g.,  Pc = 0.8 --> L = log(0.8/0.2) = log(4) so about 1.39


      nu4 <- L * (Pc^2 * L - Pc * L + Pc - 0.5) / vrt
      # getting v(hoch 4) from the EZ inversion formulas
      # rearrange EZ RT variance equation to isolate nu
      # nu^4 = L × (Pc^2 × L − Pc × L + Pc − 0.5) / VRT --> solve for nu
      # alpha  = L / nu --> get alpha
      # tau  = MRT − (alpha / 2xnu) × (2Pc − 1) --> get tau

      if (is.na(nu4) || nu4 <= 0) next # skip if  nu4 is negative or missing

      nu_hat[i, k]    <- sign(Pc - 0.5) * nu4^(1/4)
      # drift rate estimate
      # sign(Pc - 0.5) is +1 if accuracy > 50% (positive drift toward correct boundary) and −1 otherwise
      # sign returns 1 for positive values, -1 for negative values, and 0 for zero

      alpha_hat[i, k] <- L / nu_hat[i, k]
      # boundary sep estimate from EZ --> boundary = log-odds / drift rate

      tau_hat[i, k]   <- mrt - (alpha_hat[i, k] / (2 * nu_hat[i, k])) * (2 * Pc - 1)
      # NDT estimate -->  mean RT - decision time component ((alpha_hat[i, k] / (2 * nu_hat[i, k])) * (2 * Pc - 1)) = NDT
    }
  }
  list(nu = nu_hat, alpha = alpha_hat, tau = tau_hat) # put all three matrices into list
}




## function takes EZ estimates from pilot data and turns them into prior hyperparameters (that we put into stan then)
derive_priors <- function(ez) { # the input is "ez" so the list returned by by "ez_point_estimates"

  nu_vals    <- as.vector(ez$nu[!is.na(ez$nu)])
  # nu_vals = vector of all valid drift estimates (no positivity filter: negative nu is valid)
  # ez$nu = I×K matrix but as single vector

  alpha_vals <- as.vector(ez$alpha[!is.na(ez$alpha) & ez$alpha > 0])
  # same for boundary sep

  tau_vals   <- as.vector(ez$tau[!is.na(ez$tau) & ez$tau > 0.05])
  # and for NDT but here its above 0.05 and not only positive

  # nu is now on the raw scale (no log transform)
  nu_sd    <- min(max(sd(nu_vals), 0.3), 1.5)
  # compute SD of nu across participants and conditions in pilot data
  # ensure its above 0.3 and maximum 1.5 --> robustness for pilot

  alpha_sd <- min(max(sd(alpha_vals),  0.2), 1.0)
  # same here but with diff values
  tau_sd   <- min(max(sd(tau_vals),    0.1), 0.5)

  list(
    beta_nu    = matrix(c(mean(nu_vals), 0,       0,
                          nu_sd,         nu_sd,   nu_sd),
                        nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),
    # 2×3 matrix
    # row 1 = prior means for [intercept, covariate slope, condition slope] of nu
    # row 2 = prior SDs
    # intercept has mean(nu_vals) as prior mean so it is centred on what the pilot data says (raw scale)
    # slopes have 0 bc we dont know direction
    # byrow = TRUE fills matrix row by row

    beta_alpha = matrix(c(mean(alpha_vals), 0,
                          alpha_sd * 2,     alpha_sd * 2),
                        nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),
    # for alpha its 2x2 and for tau too
    beta_tau   = matrix(c(mean(tau_vals),   0,
                          tau_sd * 2,       tau_sd * 2),
                        nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),

    sigma_nu    = c(nu_sd,    nu_sd / 2), # prior for population SD of drift = normal dist with mean = nu_sd and SD = nu_sd/2
    sigma_alpha = c(alpha_sd, alpha_sd / 2),
    sigma_tau   = c(tau_sd,   tau_sd / 2),
    sigma_v     = c(nu_sd * 0.3, nu_sd) # random slope variability --> nu_sd * 0.3 and nu_sd --> much uncertainty, wide prior
  )
}

## function derives the priors from pilot aka
# that simulates separate set of pilot participants, generates data from the true parameters, and runs EZ formulas on them and then calls the function derive_priors to get the prior hyperparameters
derive_priors_from_pilot <- function(J_per, true, I_pilot = 20) {
  # J_per = trials per condition in the pilot, true = true parameters, I_pilot = how many pilot participants so 20
  K          <- 2
  cond_dummy <- c(0, 1)
  # cond 1 --> dummy variable 0 (reference)
  # cond 2 --> 1 (treatment)
  # multiplied by condition effect -->effect is zero for cond 1 and there is effect for cond 2

  x_p      <- rnorm(I_pilot, 0, 1)
  true_v_p <- rnorm(I_pilot, 0, true$sigma_v)
  # draw pilot ppns covariate values (x_p) from standard normal
  # draw pilot ppns random slope values (true_v_p) from Normal(0, sigma_v)
  # each ppn has own x and v

  # empty data matrices for the pilot participants --> filled by simulation
  J_p   <- matrix(J_per, I_pilot, K) # every cell is filled with J_per --> e.g., if J_per = 80 and I_pilot = 20, this is a 20×2 matrix of 80s
  C_p   <- matrix(NA_integer_, I_pilot, K) # placeholder I_pilot × K matrix for integers (how many correct)
  MRT_p <- matrix(NA_real_,    I_pilot, K) # same but real number because MRT
  VRT_p <- matrix(NA_real_,    I_pilot, K) # same bc VRT


  for (i in seq_len(I_pilot)) { # for ppn i
    for (k in seq_len(K)) { # in cond k
      mean_nu_ik    <- true$mu_nu + true$b1_nu * x_p[i] + true$b2_nu * cond_dummy[k]
      # computes raw-scale mean for participant i in condition k
      # = intercept + covariate effect * x + condition effect * dummy
      # for cond 1 (dummy = 0) condition effect * dummy is gone (0)

      mean_alpha_ik <- true$mu_alpha + (true$b_alpha + true_v_p[i]) * cond_dummy[k]
      # boundary sep mean per person per cond
      # = intercept + (average condition effect + this ppns adjustment) * dummy
      # again, 0 in cond 1, in cond 2 the ppns own random slope shifts boundary adjustment

      mean_tau_ik   <- true$mu_tau + true$b_tau * cond_dummy[k]
      # NDT mean per person

      repeat { a <- rnorm(1, mean_alpha_ik, true$sigma_alpha)
               if (a > 0.1 && a < 3.0) { ap <- a; break } }
      # repeat loops forever until "break" hits
      # draw alpha from normal dist and check whether it falls in the valid range, continues until valid draw and saves it (under ap)

      # nu drawn directly from normal on raw scale (negative values are valid: drift toward wrong boundary)
      np <- rnorm(1, mean_nu_ik, true$sigma_nu)

      repeat { t <- rnorm(1, mean_tau_ik, true$sigma_tau)
               if (t > 0.05) { tp <- t; break } }
      # same for tau what we did for alpha


      e      <- exp(-ap * np)
      pi_c   <- 1 / (1 + e)
      mu_rt  <- tp + (ap / (2 * np)) * ((1 - e) / (1 + e))
      sig2rt <- (ap / (2 * np^3)) * ((1 - 2*ap*np*e - e^2) / (1 + e)^2)
      # ez equations
      # given tau, alpha and nu, predict: e, predicted proportion correct, predicted mean RT for correct ones and predicted variance

      C_ik <- rbinom(1, J_per, pi_c)
      C_ik <- max(1L, min(C_ik, J_per - 1L))
      # draw number of correct responses from binomial dist (J_per trials, probability pi_c)
      # [1, J−1] again to not allow 0 or all correct because EZ formulas break then
      # 1L = integer 1


      MRT_p[i, k] <- rnorm(1, mu_rt, sqrt(sig2rt / C_ik))
      # draw observed mean RT from normal dist centred on true mean RT
      # SD is standard error of the mean RT --> gets smaller when more correct trials

      VRT_p[i, k] <- max(rnorm(1, sig2rt, sqrt(2 * sig2rt^2 / max(C_ik-1,1))), 1e-6)
      # draw observed RT variance from normal centred on true variance
      # SD --> chi-squared approximation for sample variance
      # max(..., 1e-6) so never gets negative
      # max(C_ik-1, 1) so its not diveded by zero when only 1 correct response

      C_p[i, k]   <- C_ik
    }
  }
  ez <- ez_point_estimates(C_p, J_p, MRT_p, VRT_p, I_pilot, K)
  derive_priors(ez) # runs earlier function on those estimates
}



## simulation and Stan fit
## function takes one set (I, J, priors), simulates dataset from true parameters, fits stan model and returns results
run_one <- function(I, J_per, true, model, priors,
                    rhat_threshold     = 1.05,
                    hopeless_threshold = 10,
                    iter1 = 1000, warmup1 = 300,
                    iter2 = 3000, warmup2 = 1000) {
  # I: number of ppns
  # J_per: trials per ppn per cond
  # true: "true parameter" list
  # model: stan model
  # priors: already computed prior hyperparameters for this J value
  # rhat_threshold: if any Rhat exceeds this it triggers a longer refit
  # hopeless_threshold: if Rhat exceeds 10 the fit is seen as degenerate and excluded
  # iter1 and warmup1: iterations and warmup for first run
  # iter2 and warmup2: iterations and warmup for second run if first didnt converge


  K          <- 2
  cond_dummy <- c(0, 1)
  prs <- priors #rename

  x      <- rnorm(I, 0, 1)
  true_v <- rnorm(I, 0, true$sigma_v)
  # draw ppns covariate values and random slopes
  # --> "true" individual differences


  X_nu    <- array(NA_real_, dim = c(I, K, 3))
  X_alpha <- array(NA_real_, dim = c(I, K, 2))
  X_tau   <- array(NA_real_, dim = c(I, K, 2))
  # 3 empty arrays (I × K × predictors) --> design matrices mit 3 and 2 dimensions --> tell stan what predictors each ppn in each cond has


  for (i in seq_len(I)) { # for ppn i
    for (k in seq_len(K)) { # in cond k
      X_nu[i, k, ]    <- c(1, x[i], cond_dummy[k])
      # nu predictor row is [1, x_i, cond_dummy_k]: 1 (intercept), covariate value, 0 or 1 depending on cond
      # stan multiplies row vector by [beta_nu[1], beta_nu[2], beta_nu[3]] --> we get the linear predictor for this cell
      X_alpha[i, k, ] <- c(1, cond_dummy[k])
      X_tau[i, k, ]   <- c(1, cond_dummy[k])
      # alpha and tau only have intercept + condition dummy
    }
  }
  # true parameter generation
  # same as pilot above but this time different participants (the "actual" ones)
  alpha_true <- matrix(NA_real_, I, K)
  nu_true    <- matrix(NA_real_, I, K)
  tau_true   <- matrix(NA_real_, I, K)
  # again 3 empty arrays

  for (i in seq_len(I)) { # for ppn i
    for (k in seq_len(K)) { # in cond k
      mean_nu_ik    <- true$mu_nu + true$b1_nu * x[i] + true$b2_nu * cond_dummy[k]
      # raw-scale mean for participant i in condition k

      mean_alpha_ik <- true$mu_alpha + (true$b_alpha + true_v[i]) * cond_dummy[k]
      # again boundary sep mean per person per cond

      mean_tau_ik   <- true$mu_tau + true$b_tau * cond_dummy[k]
      # and again NDT mean per ppn per cond

      repeat { a <- rnorm(1, mean_alpha_ik, true$sigma_alpha)
               if (a > 0.1 && a < 3.0) { alpha_true[i, k] <- a; break } }
      # again draw alpha from normal dist --> repeat until valid for alpha

      # nu drawn directly from normal on raw scale (no exp(), negative values valid)
      nu_true[i, k] <- rnorm(1, mean_nu_ik, true$sigma_nu)

      repeat { t <- rnorm(1, mean_tau_ik, true$sigma_tau)
               if (t > 0.05) { tau_true[i, k] <- t; break } }
      # again also draw tau and repeat until valid
    }
  }

  J_mat   <- matrix(J_per, I, K) # same as before: J_mat is filled with J_per (same number of trials for everyone)
  C_mat   <- matrix(NA_integer_, I, K) # and these are placeholder matrices again
  MRT_mat <- matrix(NA_real_,    I, K)
  VRT_mat <- matrix(NA_real_,    I, K)

  for (i in seq_len(I)) { # for ppn i
    for (k in seq_len(K)) { # in cond k
      # retrieve the true parameters for this cell, call them: a = boundary sep, v = drift, tau = NDT
      a <- alpha_true[i, k]; v <- nu_true[i, k]; tau <- tau_true[i, k]
      e      <- exp(-a * v) # when drift and boundary sep are large, a*v is large, e is near 0, when small, e is near 1
      pi_c   <- 1 / (1 + e) # predicted proportion correct from EZ

      mu_rt  <- tau + (a / (2 * v)) * ((1 - e) / (1 + e)) # predicted mean RT of correct responses
      # NDT + average time accumulator takes to hit correct boundary

      sig2rt <- (a / (2 * v^3)) * ((1 - 2*a*v*e - e^2) / (1 + e)^2) # predicted RT variance
      # gets larger when drift is slow

      # parameters are generated, now observed data generation
      # same as before, generate observed correct trials, mean RTs, RT variances from the true parameters
      C_ik <- rbinom(1, J_per, pi_c)
      C_ik <- max(1L, min(C_ik, J_per - 1L))
      # again draw observed number of correct responses from binomial dist, J_per trials, each with probability pi_c
      # again [1, J_per−1]to not allow 0 or all correct because then the formulas break

      MRT_mat[i, k] <- rnorm(1, mu_rt, sqrt(sig2rt / C_ik)) # as before
      VRT_mat[i, k] <- max(rnorm(1, sig2rt, sqrt(2 * sig2rt^2 / max(C_ik-1,1))), 1e-6) # as before
      C_mat[i, k]   <- C_ik # as before
    }
  }


  stan_data <- list(
    I = I, K = K,
    P_nu = 3L, P_alpha = 2L, P_tau = 2L,
    J = J_mat, C = C_mat, MRT = MRT_mat, VRT = VRT_mat,
    X_nu = X_nu, X_alpha = X_alpha, X_tau = X_tau,
    prior_beta_nu     = prs$beta_nu,
    prior_beta_alpha  = prs$beta_alpha,
    prior_beta_tau    = prs$beta_tau,
    prior_sigma_nu    = prs$sigma_nu,
    prior_sigma_alpha = prs$sigma_alpha,
    prior_sigma_tau   = prs$sigma_tau,
    prior_sigma_v     = prs$sigma_v
  )
  # pack everything into list for Stan
  # dimensions, observed data matrices, design matrices, prior hyperparameters
  # "L" means its integers not floating numbers --> because of stan being bitchy otherwise if we only write e.g., 3



  group_pars <- c(
    paste0("beta_nu[",    seq_len(3), "]"),
    paste0("beta_alpha[", seq_len(2), "]"),
    paste0("beta_tau[",   seq_len(2), "]"),
    "sigma_nu", "sigma_alpha", "sigma_tau", "sigma_v"
  )
  # character vector of the parameter names stan uses for the group-level parameters
  # paste0("beta_nu[", 1:3, "]") --> gets us c("beta_nu[1]", "beta_nu[2]", "beta_nu[3]")
  # to extract Rhat values from stan summary later




  hopeless <- function(fit) {
    rh <- tryCatch(summary(fit)$summary[group_pars, "Rhat"], error = function(e) NA_real_)
    any(is.na(rh)) || any(is.nan(rh)) || any(is.infinite(rh)) ||
      any(rh > hopeless_threshold, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  # helper function for hopeless cases
  # tryCatch runs what is inside of it and catches errors and then returns NA
  # extracts Rhats and returns TRUE if values are missing, NaN, infinite, or above 10
  # then they are broken


  fit <- tryCatch(
    sampling(model, data = stan_data,
             iter = iter1, warmup = warmup1, chains = 4, cores = 1, refresh = 0,
             control = list(adapt_delta = 0.85, max_treedepth = 10)),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  # drawing MCMC samples with sampling rstan function
  # runs 4 independent chains
  # refresh = 0 supresses stans progress output
  # adapt_delta --> step size (higher --> more careful --> slower)
  # max_treedepth --> how deep goes sampler tree
  # when stan crashes --> tryCatch catches error and returns NULL so it doesnt crash

  if (is.null(fit))  return(list(status = "error"))
  if (hopeless(fit)) return(list(status = "excluded", reason = "degenerate_fit1"))
  # if stan crashes --> this error is returned
  # if fit has Rhat > 10 this exclusion message is returned
  # return() exits function directly and gives out message


  rhat_max  <- max(summary(fit)$summary[group_pars, "Rhat"], na.rm = TRUE)
  converged <- "first_fit"
  if (rhat_max > rhat_threshold) {
    # extract the worst Rhat of group-level parameters
    # if > 1.05 --> fit hasn't converged well enough
    # --> has to rerun with more iterations
    # shows this message in console so I know
    message(sprintf("Refit triggered (I=%d, J=%d) — Rhat = %.2f", I, J_per, rhat_max))


    fit <- tryCatch(
      sampling(model, data = stan_data,
               iter = iter2, warmup = warmup2, chains = 4, cores = 1, refresh = 0,
               control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 12)),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )
    # refit with iter2 = 3000 warmup2 = 1000 and adapt_delta = 0.95 and max_treedepth = 12
    # stricter

    if (is.null(fit))  return(list(status = "error")) # check again like before
    if (hopeless(fit)) return(list(status = "excluded", reason = "degenerate_refit"))
    rhat_max  <- max(summary(fit)$summary[group_pars, "Rhat"], na.rm = TRUE) # also Rhats
    converged <- "refit"
    if (rhat_max > rhat_threshold)
      return(list(status = "excluded", reason = "non_converged"))
  }
  # if it still does not converge --> exclude


  s <- summary(fit)$summary
  # summary matrix --> 1 row per parameter (columns for mean, SD, quantiles, Rhat, n_eff)


  group_results <- data.frame(
    # for plotting results later --> data frame table,  one row per group-level parameter
    # row has I and J of this run, parameter name, true value, posterior mean estimate and the used prior
    # aggregated across all simulation runs
    I = I, J = J_per,
    param = c("mu_nu", "b1_nu", "b2_nu",
              "mu_alpha", "b_alpha",
              "mu_tau", "b_tau",
              "sigma_nu", "sigma_alpha", "sigma_tau", "sigma_v"),
    true_val = c(true$mu_nu,    true$b1_nu,    true$b2_nu,
                 true$mu_alpha, true$b_alpha,
                 true$mu_tau,   true$b_tau,
                 true$sigma_nu, true$sigma_alpha, true$sigma_tau, true$sigma_v),
    estimate = c(
      s["beta_nu[1]",    "mean"], s["beta_nu[2]",    "mean"], s["beta_nu[3]",  "mean"],
      s["beta_alpha[1]", "mean"], s["beta_alpha[2]", "mean"],
      s["beta_tau[1]",   "mean"], s["beta_tau[2]",   "mean"],
      s["sigma_nu",      "mean"], s["sigma_alpha",   "mean"],
      s["sigma_tau",     "mean"], s["sigma_v",       "mean"]
    ),
    prior_mean = c(
      prs$beta_nu[1,1],    prs$beta_nu[1,2],    prs$beta_nu[1,3],
      prs$beta_alpha[1,1], prs$beta_alpha[1,2],
      prs$beta_tau[1,1],   prs$beta_tau[1,2],
      prs$sigma_nu[1], prs$sigma_alpha[1], prs$sigma_tau[1], prs$sigma_v[1]
    ),
    prior_sd = c(
      prs$beta_nu[2,1],    prs$beta_nu[2,2],    prs$beta_nu[2,3],
      prs$beta_alpha[2,1], prs$beta_alpha[2,2],
      prs$beta_tau[2,1],   prs$beta_tau[2,2],
      prs$sigma_nu[2], prs$sigma_alpha[2], prs$sigma_tau[2], prs$sigma_v[2]
    ),
    converged = converged,
    rhat_max  = rhat_max,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )




  v_results <- data.frame(
    I = I, J = J_per,
    participant = seq_len(I),
    true_v = true_v,
    est_v  = s[paste0("v[", seq_len(I), "]"), "mean"]
  )
  # 1 row per participant with their true random slope and estimated random slope
  # paste0("v[", 1:I, "]") --> generates stan parameter names v[1], ... v[I]

  alpha_est <- matrix(NA_real_, I, K)
  nu_est    <- matrix(NA_real_, I, K)
  tau_est   <- matrix(NA_real_, I, K)
  # posterior mean estimates from stan --> estimation for each value
  # empty matrices with row length I and column length K to fill with estimated alpha, nu and tau
  # mirroring alpha_true, nu_true, tau_true

  for (i in seq_len(I)) { # for ppn i
    for (k in seq_len(K)) { # in cond k
      alpha_est[i, k] <- s[paste0("alpha[", i, ",", k, "]"), "mean"]
      nu_est[i, k]    <- s[paste0("nu[",    i, ",", k, "]"), "mean"]
      tau_est[i, k]   <- s[paste0("tau[",   i, ",", k, "]"), "mean"]
      # s = stan summary matrix from before  with 1 row per parameter
      # individual parameters are then called alpha[1,1], alpha[1,2], alpha[2,1] etc
      # paste0("alpha[", i, ",", k, "]") makes this exact thing --> so for i=3, k=2 its alpha[3,2]
      # the mean column extracts the posterior mean for this ppn in this condition
      # whole result is stored in alpha_est[i, k]
      # same for the tau and nu
    }
  }

  indiv_results <- data.frame(
    #  individual results data frame
    I = I, J = J_per,
    # every row gets the I and row of its run
    condition  = rep(seq_len(K), each = I), # condition column
    # seq_len(K) --> c(1, 2)
    # rep(..., each = I) repeats every value I times so --> c(1,1,...,1, 2,2,...,2)
    # as.vector() on a matrix reads column by column --> so the first I rows correspond to cond 1 and the next I rows to cond 2

    true_alpha = as.vector(alpha_true), est_alpha = as.vector(alpha_est),
    true_nu    = as.vector(nu_true),    est_nu    = as.vector(nu_est),
    true_tau   = as.vector(tau_true),   est_tau   = as.vector(tau_est)
    # as.vector() makes the I*K matrix into a vector of length I*K that first rerads column 1 and  then column 2
    # true_alpha next to est_alpha in data frame --> every row has true value and estimate for the same cell (ppn + cond)
    # need this to plot individual results later
  )
    # data frame has I*K rows per simulation run, one for each combination of participant and condition, and columns for the simulation design     (I, J), which condition it was, and the true and estimated value of each parameter
  list(status = "ok", group = group_results, v = v_results, indiv = indiv_results,
       priors_used = prs, rhat_max = rhat_max, converged = converged)
  # status = ok is later for checking successful runs and bad ones

}


## compile Stan model
cache_file <- paste0(tools::file_path_sans_ext(
  "new_corrected_model_w_cond_and_slopes_2.stan"), ".rds")
if (file.exists(cache_file)) file.remove(cache_file)
# forces a fresh recompile --> not using old compiled version if edited

## derive priors once per J value
set.seed(42) # reproducible
priors_by_J <- setNames(
  lapply(J_vals, function(j) derive_priors_from_pilot(j, true, I_pilot = 20)),
  # applies function to each element of J_vals --> returns list with 3 results
  as.character(J_vals) # names the list elements "20", etc so they can be looked up again
)
# priors_by_J[["20"]], priors_by_J[["60"]] and priors_by_J[["160"]] each contains set of prior hyperparameters that are derived from 20 participants at that J



## parallel simulation
jobs      <- expand.grid(I = I_vals, J = J_vals, sim = seq_len(N_sim))
# expand.grid creates 3 I values × 3 J values × 60 simulations = data frame with 540 rows --> one per job

jobs_list <- split(jobs, seq_len(nrow(jobs)))
## splits data frame into a list of one-row data frames, each worker gets one element of list

cl <- makeCluster(detectCores() - 1)
## makes cluster of worker processes --> detectCores() --> how many CPU cores --> uses all besides one

clusterSetRNGStream(cl, 42)
## parallel safe random number streams for all workers, seeded
## otherwise all workers would use the same random numbers

clusterExport(cl, varlist = c("run_one", "derive_priors_from_pilot",
                              "ez_point_estimates", "derive_priors",
                              "true", "priors_by_J"))
# sends objects from session to every worker
# workers = separate processes with empty environments without knowledge from session


clusterEvalQ(cl, {
  library(rstan)
  library(dplyr)
  rstan_options(auto_write = FALSE)
  options(mc.cores = 1)
  ez_cond <<- stan_model("new_corrected_model_w_cond_and_slopes_2.stan")
})
## each worker loads stan, compiles model into ez_cond, and sets mc.cores = 1 so stan doesn't use multiple cores from within a worker
## "<<-" assigns to the global environment of the worker



results_list <- parLapply(cl, jobs_list, function(row) {
  run_one(I      = row$I,
          J_per  = row$J,
          true   = true,
          model  = ez_cond,
          priors = priors_by_J[[as.character(row$J)]])
})
# parallel lappply
# distribute jobs across workers, each calls run_one function with  I, J, and priors and returns list of results


stopCluster(cl)
# shut down the worker processes in the end

saveRDS(results_list, file = "output_new/simulation_results.rds")
# save results






## plotting

# gather results
ok_idx        <- sapply(results_list, function(r) !is.null(r) && r$status == "ok")
# create vector of TRUE (run succeeded) or FALSE
# !is.null(r) guard against NULL (worker crash)
# r$status == "ok" checks whether run has the status ok or not

ok_results    <- results_list[ok_idx]
results_group <- bind_rows(lapply(ok_results, `[[`, "group"))
# only the successful runs
# lapply(..., "[[", "group") extracts group data frame from each result --> stacks all data frames vertically into one big data frame --> one row per parameter per simulation run

results_v     <- bind_rows(lapply(ok_results, `[[`, "v")) # same here and
results_indiv <- bind_rows(lapply(ok_results, `[[`, "indiv")) # here

# exclusion report
# counts how many runs fall into each category --> sum() count of TRUE
n_total    <- length(results_list)
n_ok       <- sum(ok_idx)
n_excluded <- sum(sapply(results_list, function(r) !is.null(r) && r$status == "excluded"))
n_error    <- sum(sapply(results_list, function(r) is.null(r)  || r$status == "error"))
print(data.frame(
  Total = n_total, Converged = n_ok, Excluded = n_excluded, Error = n_error,
  `Excluded (%)` = round(100 * n_excluded / n_total, 1), check.names = FALSE
))


# exclusion breakdown by cell
status_df <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(results_list), function(i) {
  r <- results_list[[i]]; row <- jobs[i, ]
  data.frame(I = row$I, J = row$J, sim = row$sim,
             status = if (is.null(r)) "error" else r$status,
             reason = if (is.null(r) || r$status == "ok") NA else r$reason)
}))


status_df %>%
  group_by(I, J) %>%
  summarise(n        = n(),
            excluded = sum(status == "excluded"),
            pct      = round(100 * excluded / n, 1),
            reasons  = paste(table(reason[status == "excluded"]), collapse = ", "),
            .groups  = "drop") %>%
  print(n = Inf)
# summarises separately for each I×J combination, n() counts rows in the group --> table exclusion rates per cell



# factor labels for plots
add_labels <- function(df) {
  df %>% mutate(
    I_label = factor(paste0("I = ", I), levels = paste0("I = ", I_vals)),
    J_label = factor(paste0("J = ", J), levels = paste0("J = ", J_vals))
  )
}
results_group <- add_labels(results_group)
results_v     <- add_labels(results_v)
results_indiv <- results_indiv %>%
  add_labels() %>%
  mutate(condition = factor(condition, labels = c("Condition 1 (k=1)", "Condition 2 (k=2)")))

# theme for plots
dark_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.background   = element_rect(fill = "#1e1e1e", colour = NA),
    panel.background  = element_rect(fill = "#1e1e1e", colour = NA),
    panel.grid.major  = element_line(colour = "#333333"),
    panel.grid.minor  = element_blank(),
    text              = element_text(colour = "white"),
    axis.text         = element_text(colour = "white"),
    strip.text        = element_text(colour = "white"),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "#1e1e1e"),
    legend.text       = element_text(colour = "white")
  )
save_plot <- function(plot, filename, width = 8, height = 6) {
  ggsave(file.path("output_new", filename), plot, width = width, height = height,
         dpi = 300, bg = "#1e1e1e")
}

# group-level bias plots
plot_group_bias <- function(param_name, label) {
  df <- results_group %>%
    filter(param == param_name) %>%
    mutate(bias = estimate - true_val)
  ggplot(df, aes(x = J_label, y = bias)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_violin(fill = "goldenrod", colour = NA, alpha = 0.35, trim = TRUE, scale = "width") +
    geom_jitter(colour = "goldenrod", alpha = 0.7, size = 1.4, width = 0.08) +
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "crossbar", colour = "white",
                 linewidth = 0.6, width = 0.4, fatten = 1) +
    facet_grid(I_label ~ .) +
    labs(title = label, x = "Trials per condition", y = "Bias (estimate − true)") +
    dark_theme
}
p_mu_nu    <- plot_group_bias("mu_nu",    expression(mu^(nu)~"(intercept, raw scale)"))
p_mu_alpha <- plot_group_bias("mu_alpha", expression(mu^(alpha)))
p_mu_tau   <- plot_group_bias("mu_tau",   expression(mu^(tau)))
p_b1_nu    <- plot_group_bias("b1_nu",    expression(beta[1]^(nu)~"(covariate effect on drift)"))
p_b2_nu    <- plot_group_bias("b2_nu",    expression(beta[2]^(nu)~"(condition effect on drift)"))
p_b_alpha  <- plot_group_bias("b_alpha",  expression(beta^(alpha)~"(avg condition effect)"))
p_b_tau    <- plot_group_bias("b_tau",    expression(beta^(tau)~"(condition)"))
p_sigma_v  <- plot_group_bias("sigma_v",  expression(sigma[v]~"(random slope SD)"))
for (p in list(p_mu_nu, p_mu_alpha, p_mu_tau,
               p_b1_nu, p_b2_nu, p_b_alpha, p_b_tau, p_sigma_v)) print(p)
save_plot(p_mu_nu,    "bias_mu_nu.png");    save_plot(p_mu_alpha, "bias_mu_alpha.png")
save_plot(p_mu_tau,   "bias_mu_tau.png");   save_plot(p_b1_nu,    "bias_b1_nu.png")
save_plot(p_b2_nu,    "bias_b2_nu.png");    save_plot(p_b_alpha,  "bias_b_alpha.png")
save_plot(p_b_tau,    "bias_b_tau.png");    save_plot(p_sigma_v,  "bias_sigma_v.png")

# individual-level recovery plots
plot_indiv_recovery <- function(true_col, est_col, label) {
  ggplot(results_indiv, aes_string(x = true_col, y = est_col, colour = "condition")) +
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1,
                linetype = "dashed", colour = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.35, size = 0.9) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("Condition 1 (k=1)" = "goldenrod",
                                   "Condition 2 (k=2)" = "steelblue")) +
    facet_grid(I_label ~ J_label) +
    labs(title = label, x = paste("True", label), y = paste("Estimated", label),
         colour = "Condition") +
    dark_theme + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
p_indiv_alpha <- plot_indiv_recovery("true_alpha", "est_alpha", expression(alpha[ik]))
p_indiv_nu    <- plot_indiv_recovery("true_nu",    "est_nu",    expression(nu[ik]))
p_indiv_tau   <- plot_indiv_recovery("true_tau",   "est_tau",   expression(tau[ik]))
for (p in list(p_indiv_alpha, p_indiv_nu, p_indiv_tau)) print(p)
save_plot(p_indiv_alpha, "recovery_alpha.png", width = 10, height = 8)
save_plot(p_indiv_nu,    "recovery_nu.png",    width = 10, height = 8)
save_plot(p_indiv_tau,   "recovery_tau.png",   width = 10, height = 8)

# random slope recovery plot
p_v_recovery <- ggplot(results_v, aes(x = true_v, y = est_v)) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1,
              linetype = "dashed", colour = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(colour = "goldenrod", alpha = 0.4, size = 1.2) +
  facet_grid(I_label ~ J_label) +
  labs(title = expression("Recovery of by-participant random slopes " * v[i]),
       x = "True v", y = "Estimated v") +
  dark_theme
print(p_v_recovery)
save_plot(p_v_recovery, "recovery_v.png", width = 10, height = 8)

# prior summary table
prior_summary <- results_group %>%
  group_by(param, I, J) %>%
  summarise(`Prior mean (avg)` = round(mean(prior_mean, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            `Prior SD (avg)`   = round(mean(prior_sd,   na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  rename(Parameter = param)
write.csv(prior_summary, file.path("output_new", "prior_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
kable(prior_summary,
      caption = "average derived prior hyperparameters across simulations,
                 by parameter, number of participants, and trials per condition.")
```

```{r small try out sim for different nus}
library(rstan)
library(ggplot2)
rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)
options(mc.cores = 1)

# ── test grid ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
mu_nu_vals <- c(-0.5, -0.2, 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.8)  # true population drift rates to test
I     <- 20   # small -- just for testing
J_per <- 60
K     <- 2
set.seed(99)

# ── fixed nuisance true parameters ────────────────────────────────────────────
true_fixed <- list(
  b1_nu    = 0.0,   # no covariate effect for simplicity
  b2_nu    = 0.0,   # no condition effect for simplicity
  mu_alpha = 1.5,
  b_alpha  = 0.0,
  mu_tau   = 0.3,
  b_tau    = 0.0,
  sigma_nu    = 0.3,
  sigma_alpha = 0.25,
  sigma_tau   = 0.15,
  sigma_v     = 0.1
)

# ── flat/wide priors (not pilot-derived, just for the test) ───────────────────
make_priors <- function() {
  list(
    beta_nu    = matrix(c(0, 0, 0,
                          1, 1, 1), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),
    beta_alpha = matrix(c(1.5, 0,
                          0.5, 0.5), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),
    beta_tau   = matrix(c(0.3, 0,
                          0.3, 0.3), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),
    sigma_nu    = c(0.3, 0.3),
    sigma_alpha = c(0.3, 0.2),
    sigma_tau   = c(0.2, 0.1),
    sigma_v     = c(0.1, 0.1)
  )
}

# ── data generator ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
gen_data <- function(mu_nu, true) {
  cond_dummy <- c(0, 1)
  x      <- rnorm(I, 0, 1)
  true_v <- rnorm(I, 0, true$sigma_v)
  
  X_nu    <- array(NA_real_, dim = c(I, K, 3))
  X_alpha <- array(NA_real_, dim = c(I, K, 2))
  X_tau   <- array(NA_real_, dim = c(I, K, 2))
  for (i in seq_len(I)) for (k in seq_len(K)) {
    X_nu[i,k,]    <- c(1, x[i], cond_dummy[k])
    X_alpha[i,k,] <- c(1, cond_dummy[k])
    X_tau[i,k,]   <- c(1, cond_dummy[k])
  }
  
  J_mat <- matrix(J_per, I, K)
  C_mat <- matrix(NA_integer_, I, K)
  MRT   <- matrix(NA_real_, I, K)
  VRT   <- matrix(NA_real_, I, K)
  
  for (i in seq_len(I)) for (k in seq_len(K)) {
    nu_ik    <- rnorm(1, mu_nu + true$b1_nu*x[i] + true$b2_nu*cond_dummy[k], true$sigma_nu)
    alpha_ik <- NA; repeat { a <- rnorm(1, true$mu_alpha, true$sigma_alpha); if (a > 0.1 && a < 3) { alpha_ik <- a; break } }
    tau_ik   <- NA; repeat { t <- rnorm(1, true$mu_tau,   true$sigma_tau);   if (t > 0.05)         { tau_ik   <- t; break } }
    
    e      <- exp(-alpha_ik * nu_ik)
    pi_c   <- 1 / (1 + e)
    mu_rt  <- tau_ik + (alpha_ik / (2*nu_ik)) * ((1-e)/(1+e))
    sig2rt <- (alpha_ik / (2*nu_ik^3)) * ((1 - 2*alpha_ik*nu_ik*e - e^2) / (1+e)^2)
    sig2rt <- max(sig2rt, 1e-6)   # same guard as Stan
    
    C_ik        <- max(1L, min(rbinom(1, J_per, pi_c), J_per - 1L))
    MRT[i,k]    <- rnorm(1, mu_rt,  sqrt(sig2rt / C_ik))
    VRT[i,k]    <- max(rnorm(1, sig2rt, sqrt(2*sig2rt^2 / max(C_ik-1,1))), 1e-6)
    C_mat[i,k]  <- C_ik
  }
  
  prs <- make_priors()
  list(
    stan_data = list(
      I=I, K=K, P_nu=3L, P_alpha=2L, P_tau=2L,
      J=J_mat, C=C_mat, MRT=MRT, VRT=VRT,
      X_nu=X_nu, X_alpha=X_alpha, X_tau=X_tau,
      prior_beta_nu=prs$beta_nu, prior_beta_alpha=prs$beta_alpha, prior_beta_tau=prs$beta_tau,
      prior_sigma_nu=prs$sigma_nu, prior_sigma_alpha=prs$sigma_alpha,
      prior_sigma_tau=prs$sigma_tau, prior_sigma_v=prs$sigma_v
    ),
    priors = prs
  )
}

# ── compile once ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
model <- stan_model("new_corrected_model_w_cond_and_slopes_2.stan")

# ── fit loop ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
results <- lapply(mu_nu_vals, function(mu_nu) {
  cat(sprintf("\n=== true mu_nu = %.2f ===\n", mu_nu))
  d   <- gen_data(mu_nu, true_fixed)
  fit <- sampling(model, data = d$stan_data,
                  iter = 1500, warmup = 500, chains = 2, cores = 1, refresh = 0,
                  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.90, max_treedepth = 10))
  s   <- summary(fit)$summary
  data.frame(
    true_mu_nu = mu_nu,
    est        = s["beta_nu[1]", "mean"],
    lo         = s["beta_nu[1]", "2.5%"],
    hi         = s["beta_nu[1]", "97.5%"],
    rhat       = s["beta_nu[1]", "Rhat"]
  )
})

df <- do.call(rbind, results)
print(df)

# ── plot ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ggplot(df, aes(x = true_mu_nu, y = est)) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = 0.04, colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(size = 3, colour = "goldenrod") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("Rhat=%.3f", rhat)),
            vjust = -1, size = 3, colour = "white") +
  labs(title = "Recovery of mu_nu across the sign boundary",
       subtitle = "Points = posterior mean, bars = 95% CI, dashed = identity",
       x = "True mu_nu", y = "Estimated beta_nu[1]") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#1e1e1e", colour = NA),
        panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#1e1e1e", colour = NA),
        panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "#333333"),
        text = element_text(colour = "white"),
        axis.text = element_text(colour = "white"))
```
